# CANDIDATE: LEVEL_SWEEP_AND_HOLD_WITH_VWAP_FILTER

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Price often sweeps a named level (prior day high/low) to trigger stop-runs, then holds inside the level when the sweep lacks follow-through, offering a reversal opportunity aligned with VWAP. This edge exists because liquidity providers often engineer false breakouts to capture stop-loss orders, then allow price to revert to fair value (VWAP) when the sweep fails to attract follow-through momentum.

## Mechanism

Entry rule: Identify a named level (prior day’s high for shorts, low for longs). If price penetrates the level by > 0.1% (sweep) on a 5-min bar but then closes back inside the level on the same bar with a body > 50% of the range and close > VWAP (for long) or close < VWAP (for short), then enter at the close of that bar in the direction opposite the sweep (long after a low-sweep, short after a high-sweep). Exit shape: Stop = extreme of the sweep bar (the high for short, low for long); target = 1.5× risk, with a breaker‑stop at VWAP if price re‑crosses VWAP against the trade. Regime hint: Works when VIX > 22 (elevated volatility) increasing likelihood of false breakouts, and during the mid‑morning window (10:00‑11:30 ET) when liquidity providers are active.
